newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels says unlucky June hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels says unlucky June hurt Q2.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc said Tuesday its lower than expected wins in June at the Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City was largely responsible for its second quarter loss.
Bruce McKee, senior vice president of corporate finance, said the company needed $6.3 million more in revenues to eliminate its loss for the quarter and turn a small profit.
McKee said the company did not make that $6.3 million because its percentage of games fell lower than the industry average of 15.5 percent, particularly in June.
"We're basically trying to say we played a little unlucky in June," McKee said
Because of that bad luck, the company made $4.9 million less than it expected in June alone, McKee said. $3.5 million of that $4.9 million lower than expected revenue was due to the Taj Mahal.
The Taj Mahal reported net revenues of $147.0 million compared to $140.8 million. Trump Plaza, also in Atlantic City, reported revenues of $109.5 million compared to $106.4 million.
